# iPad app window device independence (2026-01-24 16:47Z)

_**User**_

on my  ipad device I still cannot open up two separate app windows that can show different devices - if i select a device in one window it will be selected/shown in both

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPad_RootView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct iPad_RootView: View {\n    @ObservedObject private var settings = SettingsManager.shared\n    @State private var selectedTab = 0\n\n    var body: some View {\n        TabView(selection: $selectedTab) {\n            iPad_DevicesView()\n                .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"devices\", systemImage: \"iphone.gen3.badge.location\")\n                }\n                .tag(0)\n            iPad_GroupsView()\n                .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"groups\", systemImage: \"person.3\")\n                }\n                .tag(1)\n            iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView()\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"qr\", systemImage: \"qrcode\")\n                }\n                .tag(2)\n            iPhone_SettingsView()\n                .navigationViewStyle(.stack)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"settings\", systemImage: \"gear\")\n                }\n                .tag(3)\n        }\n        .environmentObject(DeviceGroupStore.shared)\n        .environmentObject(RouteInfoState.shared)\n        .environmentObject(SettingsManager.shared)\n        .bottomAccessory(onTap: nil)\n        .ignoresSafeArea(.all)\n        .toolbarBackground(.clear, for: .tabBar)\n        .toolbarBackground(.clear, for: .navigationBar)\n        .toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.visible, for: .tabBar)\n        .toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.visible, for: .navigationBar)\n        .onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID) { _, newValue in\n            if newValue != nil {\n                selectedTab = 0\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    iPad_RootView()\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./APP_FEATURES.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 28

        },
        "contents": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\n\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\n\n## App Navigation and Views\n**For users:**\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\n\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\n\n## Location Tracking\n**For users:**\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\n\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

          {
            "text": "## Location Tracking",

          },
          {
            "text": "**For users:**",

          {

        "contents": "**For developers:**\n- &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &#96;Application Support&#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly. A &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; caches routes by device and transport, with distance‑based invalidation.\n- Static map elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96; and &#96;DeviceNameLabel&#96; are rasterized and cached with keys that include color scheme and display scale; renderers respect Dynamic Type and set &#96;isOpaque=false&#96; where appropriate.\n\n## Haptic Feedback and UI Enhancements\n**For users:**\n- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle haptic feedback, pulsing accuracy circles show location precision, and shimmering indicators highlight loading states.\n\n- Animations for pulsing/shimmer are automatically reduced in Low Power Mode or when the app is backgrounded to save energy.\n\n**For developers:**\n- The &#96;Haptic&#96; utility abstracts platform differences. Shared UI elements such as &#96;MiataruMapMarker&#96;, &#96;PulsingAccuracyCircle&#96;, &#96;Shimmer&#96;, &#96;MapCompass&#96;, and &#96;MapScaleBar&#96; reside under &#96;views/Common&#96; and are reused across device and group map views.\n\n## Multi‑platform Support\n**For users:**\n- The interface adapts to iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with platform‑specific root views and onboarding flows. iPhone uses a tab bar, iPad presents split views, and Mac currently mirrors the iPhone experience in a resizable window.\n\n- On iPad, you can open device details in separate windows for multitasking.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects the appropriate root view using size classes and platform checks. Dedicated onboarding containers exist for each platform, and many components in &#96;views/Common&#96; are platform agnostic.\n\n## Localization and Accessibility\n**For users:**\n- Available in English, German, and Japanese, with dynamic type and accessibility labels and hints applied to buttons, tab items, and swipe actions.\n\n- VoiceOver support has been improved across lists and map controls. Alerts and route‑limit messages are localized.",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPhone_RootView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct iPhone_RootView: View {\n    @ObservedObject private var settings = SettingsManager.shared\n    @State private var selectedTab = 0\n\n    var body: some View {\n        TabView(selection: $selectedTab) {\n            iPhone_DevicesView()\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"devices\", systemImage: \"iphone.gen3.badge.location\")\n                }\n                .tag(0)\n            iPhone_GroupsView()\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"groups\", systemImage: \"person.3\")\n                }\n                .tag(1)\n            iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView()\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"qr\", systemImage: \"qrcode\")\n                }\n                .tag(2)\n            iPhone_SettingsView()\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"settings\", systemImage: \"gear\")\n                }\n                .tag(3)\n        }\n        .environmentObject(DeviceGroupStore.shared)\n        .environmentObject(RouteInfoState.shared)\n        .environmentObject(SettingsManager.shared)\n        .bottomAccessory(onTap: nil)\n        .adaptiveToolbarBackground()\n        .onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID) { _, newValue in\n            if newValue != nil {\n                selectedTab = 0\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    iPhone_RootView()\n}",

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

                  "lineNumber": 15977,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"The core issue is likely that on cold launch, &amp;amp;#96;.onOpenURL&amp;amp;#96; may not be called promptly or at all, so handling the URL in AppDelegate’s launch options and &amp;amp;#96;application(_:open:)&amp;amp;#96; can reliably capture deep links early.         "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * iPad_RootView.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\nstruct iPad_RootView: View {\n    @ObservedObject private var settings = SettingsManager.shared\n    @State private var selectedTab = 0\n\n    var body: some View {\n        TabView(selection: $selectedTab) {\n            iPad_DevicesView()\n                .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"devices\", systemImage: \"iphone.gen3.badge.location\")\n                }\n                .tag(0)\n            iPad_GroupsView()\n                .ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .top)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"groups\", systemImage: \"person.3\")\n                }\n                .tag(1)\n            iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView()\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"qr\", systemImage: \"qrcode\")\n                }\n                .tag(2)\n            iPhone_SettingsView()\n                .navigationViewStyle(.stack)\n                .tabItem {\n                    Label(\"settings\", systemImage: \"gear\")\n                }\n                .tag(3)\n        }\n        .environmentObject(DeviceGroupStore.shared)\n        .environmentObject(RouteInfoState.shared)\n        .environmentObject(SettingsManager.shared)\n        .bottomAccessory(onTap: nil)\n        .ignoresSafeArea(.all)\n        .toolbarBackground(.clear, for: .tabBar)\n        .toolbarBackground(.clear, for: .navigationBar)\n        .toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.visible, for: .tabBar)\n        .toolbarBackgroundVisibility(.visible, for: .navigationBar)\n        .onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID) { _, newValue in\n            if newValue != nil {\n                selectedTab = 0\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#Preview {\n    iPad_RootView()\n}",

## Zusammenfassung der Lösung

**Problem:** Wenn in einem iPad-Fenster ein Gerät ausgewählt wird, wird `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` aktualisiert, was `onChange` in allen Fenstern auslöst und alle Fenster synchronisiert.

**Lösung:**
1. Neuer Parameter `isFromLocalSelection` in `iPad_DeviceMapView`, um lokale Auswahl zu erkennen.
2. `onAppear` in `iPad_DeviceMapView` aktualisiert `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` nur, wenn es sich nicht um eine lokale Auswahl handelt.
3. `isLocalSelectionChange`-Flag in `iPad_DevicesView`, um lokale Benutzerauswahl von Deep-Link-Änderungen zu unterscheiden.

<reproduction_steps>
1. App auf dem iPad starten
2. Zwei separate App-Fenster öffnen (z. B. durch Teilen des Bildschirms oder Öffnen eines zweiten Fensters)
3. In Fenster 1 ein Gerät auswählen (z. B. "Device A")
4. In Fenster 2 ein anderes Gerät auswählen (z. B. "Device B")
5. Prüfen, ob beide Fenster unterschiedliche Geräte anzeigen (Fenster 1 sollte "Device A" zeigen, Fenster 2 sollte "Device B" zeigen)
6. In Fenster 1 ein anderes Gerät auswählen (z. B. "Device C")
7. Prüfen, ob Fenster 2 weiterhin "Device B" zeigt und nicht automatisch zu "Device C" wechselt
</reproduction_steps>

Bitte die App neu starten, damit die Änderungen wirksam werden. Falls das Problem weiterhin besteht, analysiere ich die Debug-Logs, um die Ursache zu finden.

Problem: `isLocalSelectionChange` ist in den Logs immer `false`, weil die View erstellt wird, bevor `onChange(of: selection)` den Flag setzt. Zudem wird `isFromLocalSelection` zum Zeitpunkt der View-Erstellung gelesen, wenn der Flag noch nicht gesetzt ist.

Neue Hypothesen:
1. `isFromLocalSelection` wird zum falschen Zeitpunkt gelesen (vor dem Setzen des Flags).
2. `onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID)` wird trotzdem ausgelöst und synchronisiert die Fenster.
3. Die Bedingung `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID != newSelection` greift nicht, weil der Wert bereits gesetzt ist.

Lösung: `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` nicht in `onAppear` aktualisieren, wenn die Änderung von einer lokalen Auswahl stammt. Stattdessen prüfen, ob die Änderung von `onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID)` kommt.

---


Problem: Die View wird erstellt, bevor `onChange(of: selection)` den Flag setzt, daher ist `isLocalSelectionChange` zum Zeitpunkt der View-Erstellung noch `false`.

Lösung: `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` nicht in `onAppear` aktualisieren, wenn die Änderung von einer lokalen Auswahl stammt. Stattdessen prüfen, ob die Änderung von `onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID)` kommt, und nur dann aktualisieren.

Einfachere Lösung: `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` in `onAppear` nur aktualisieren, wenn es sich um einen Deep-Link handelt (d. h. wenn `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` bereits auf den neuen Wert gesetzt ist, bevor die View erscheint).

## Zusammenfassung der Lösung

**Problem:** Wenn in einem iPad-Fenster ein Gerät ausgewählt wird, wird `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` aktualisiert, was `onChange` in allen Fenstern auslöst und alle Fenster synchronisiert.

**Lösung:**
1. `isUpdatingFromDeepLink`-Flag: Unterscheidet zwischen lokaler Benutzerauswahl und Deep-Link-Änderungen.
2. `shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID` wird dynamisch gesetzt:
   - `false` für lokale Auswahlen (verhindert Cross-Window-Sync)
   - `true` für Deep-Links (erlaubt Deep-Link-Updates)
3. `onChange(of: selection)` aktualisiert `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` nicht mehr bei lokalen Auswahlen.

**Änderungen:**
- `iPad_DevicesView`: Verwendet `isUpdatingFromDeepLink`, um zu erkennen, ob die Änderung von einem Deep-Link kommt
- `iPad_DeviceMapView`: Erhält `shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID` basierend auf `isUpdatingFromDeepLink`
- `onChange(of: settings.lastOpenedDeviceID)`: Setzt `isUpdatingFromDeepLink = true` für Deep-Links

<reproduction_steps>
1. App auf dem iPad neu starten (damit die Änderungen wirksam werden)
2. Zwei separate App-Fenster öffnen
3. In Fenster 1 ein Gerät auswählen (z. B. "Device A")
4. In Fenster 2 ein anderes Gerät auswählen (z. B. "Device B")
5. Prüfen, ob beide Fenster unterschiedliche Geräte anzeigen (Fenster 1 sollte "Device A" zeigen, Fenster 2 sollte "Device B" zeigen)
6. In Fenster 1 ein anderes Gerät auswählen (z. B. "Device C")
7. Prüfen, ob Fenster 2 weiterhin "Device B" zeigt und nicht automatisch zu "Device C" wechselt
</reproduction_steps>

Bitte die App neu starten und testen. Die Debug-Logs sind aktiv und helfen bei der Analyse, falls das Problem weiterhin besteht.

## Entfernte Instrumentierung

1. **iPad_DevicesView.swift:**
   - Entfernt: Logging in `onChange(of: selection)`
   - Entfernt: Logging für lokale vs. Deep-Link-Auswahl

2. **iPad_DeviceMapView.swift:**
   - Entfernt: Logging in `onAppear`
   - Entfernt: Logging beim Setzen von `lastOpenedDeviceID`

3. **Debug-Log-Datei gelöscht**

## Finale Lösung (ohne Instrumentierung)

Die Lösung bleibt aktiv:
- `isUpdatingFromDeepLink` unterscheidet zwischen lokaler Auswahl und Deep-Links
- `shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID` wird dynamisch basierend auf `isUpdatingFromDeepLink` gesetzt
- Lokale Auswahlen aktualisieren `settings.lastOpenedDeviceID` nicht mehr, was Cross-Window-Synchronisation verhindert

Die App sollte jetzt korrekt funktionieren: Jedes iPad-Fenster kann unabhängig ein Gerät anzeigen, ohne dass die Auswahl in anderen Fenstern synchronisiert wird.
